claim.pdf_says: Clause 10 is 'Structured compilation group' with same-level subclauses 10.1 General, 10.2 Compilation units, 10.3 Source units, 10.4 Contained source units, 10.5 Source elements and runtime elements, 10.6 COBOL compilation group, 10.7 End markers - all printed at the identical heading weight/indent, with 10.6.1/10.6.2/10.6.3 and 10.7.1-10.7.4 one level below.
claim.markdown_says: The transcription splits the level: '## 10 Structured compilation group' (line 12330), '### 10.1 General' (12333), '### 10.2 Compilation units' (12338), '### 10.3 Source units' (12356), then '## 10.4 Contained source units' (12395), '## 10.5 Source elements and runtime elements' (12408), '## 10.6 COBOL compilation group' (12439), '### 10.6.1 General format' (12442), '## 10.6.2  Syntax rules' (12641), '## 10.6.3 General rule' (12675), '## 10.7 End markers' (12689) with '### 10.7.1 General' (12692).
claim.why_it_matters: 10.4, 10.5, 10.6 and 10.7 are rendered at the same markdown level as clause 10 itself, so in any generated outline they become siblings of the clause rather than its subclauses; 10.6.2 and 10.6.3 are rendered ABOVE their own sibling 10.6.1 in the hierarchy (## vs ###), which detaches them from 10.6. Section navigation and any TOC built from the markdown misrepresent the standard's clause tree.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED. (1) Nothing is missing. Rendered page 285 at 300 dpi (printed page 255) prints exactly two headings, 'Contained source units' and 'Source elements and runtime elements', numbered 10.4 and 10.5, and the markdown carries both verbatim with correct numbers, correct order, and correct hierarchical anchors <a id="section-10-4"> and <a id="section-10-5">. The kind label 'missing-heading' is a misnomer: the only difference is the count of '#' characters, i.e. markdown markup, which the rejection criteria list as formatting. (2) The claim misdescribes the PDF. It asserts clause 10 and its subclauses are 'all printed at the identical heading weight/indent'. They are not. On rendered page 284 the clause title '10 Structured compilation group' is set in a visibly LARGER SANS-SERIF bold face, while '10.1 General', '10.2 Compilation units' and '10.3 Source units' below it are serif bold at body size. The PDF therefore does distinguish the clause from its subclauses, and the two-level markdown split of 10 vs 10.1-10.3 actually MATCHES the print. What the PDF does not distinguish is depth BELOW that: on page 286 '10.6 COBOL compilation group' and '10.6.1 General format' are the same serif bold face and indent, and on page 289 '10.6.2  Syntax rules' is that same face - so the print conveys 10.6 vs 10.6.1 nesting solely by the clause NUMBER, which the markdown preserves character for character. (3) The markdown '#' depth is page-local by construction and never encoded a document clause tree, so there is no faithful outline for this to corrupt. 1261 of the 2303 level-2 headings in specs/ISO_COBOL.md are '## Page NNN' markers, and the running header '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' occupies level 1. Clause 10 is already a '##' sibling of '## Page 284'. The depth resets at each page boundary throughout the document, not just here: page 282 shows '## 9.3.13', '## 9.3.14', '### 9.3.14.1', '## 9.4'; within clause 10 the reset lands on 10.4 (first heading on p285), 10.6.2 (first on p289), 10.6.3 (first on p290) and 10.7 (first on p291) - precisely the headings the claim flags. This is a systemic property of the page-by-page transcription, not a content defect on page 285. (4) Navigation and citation are unaffected. Every subclause in the range carries a hierarchy-correct anchor (section-10, section-10-1 .. section-10-7, section-10-6-1, section-10-6-2, section-10-6-3, section-10-7-1 ..), and this project cites the standard by clause number ('8.4.6, Scope of names' on this very page), never by markdown nesting depth. No semantic content, no clause number, no heading text, and no normative statement differs between the PDF and the transcription. The one residual nit visible in the quoted markdown is the double space in '## 10.6.2  Syntax rules', which is whitespace transcription of the PDF's wide tab gap after the clause number - also not content.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a PDF-vs-markdown content discrepancy. Page 285's two headings (10.4 Contained source units, 10.5 Source elements and runtime elements) are present verbatim with correct numbers, order and section anchors. The claim's premise about the print is wrong: clause 10's title IS set in a larger sans-serif face distinct from its serif-bold subclause headings, so the '## 10' / '### 10.1' split matches the PDF. The varying '#' depth for 10.4, 10.5, 10.6.2, 10.6.3 and 10.7 is the transcription's document-wide page-local heading convention - depth restarts at each '## Page NNN' marker, and 1261 of 2303 level-2 headings ARE those page markers - so markdown depth is not, and was never, a semantic clause tree anywhere in the file. If a semantic outline is ever wanted it must be generated globally from the clause numbers or the section-N-N-N anchors (both complete and correct), not patched page by page; that is a tooling choice, not a page-285 transcription error.
